Study the following information carefully and answer the questions accordingly.

 

In a certain code language,

`moving back facing side` is written as `ygb okz uno rml`

`car moving too fast`  is written as `alg ygb hah has`

`time come back may` is written as `ldt wik okz fay`

`come facing problem start` is written as ` wik uno slv ggg`

 

In the given code language, what does the code 'ygb' stand for?
questions.explanation:
moving = ygb

back =okz

facing = uno

side = rml

come = wik

car =  alg / hah / has

too = alg / hah / has

fast = alg / hah / has

time = ldt / fay

may = ldt / fay

problem = slv / ggg

start = slv / ggg

`moving back facing side` →`  ygb okz uno rml`   …(1)

` car moving too fast`  →` alg ygb hah has`   …(2)

`time come back may` →` ldt wik okz fay`   …(3)

`come facing problem start` →` wik uno slv ggg`   …(4)

from 1 and 2, we get   …(5)

moving = ygb

from 1 and 3, we get  …(6)

back =okz

from 1 and 4, we get   …(7)

facing = uno

from 1, 5, 6 and 7 , we get

side = rml

from 3 and 4, we get

come = wik

Read the given information carefully and answer the questions given below:

 

Eight persons- M, N, O, P, Q, R, S and T attend the yoga classes on two different dates either 15 or 22 of four different months – January, April, September and December of the same year. They attend the yoga classes in different cities- Delhi, Panipat, Lucknow, Ranchi, Haridwar, Bhopal, Indore and Patna. All the information is not necessarily in the same order.
Three persons attend the yoga classes between M and the one who attends the yoga class in Bhopal. M attends the class in the month having even number of days. O attends just after the one who attends yoga class in Bhopal. More than three persons attend the yoga classes between O and T. O and T attend the classes on the same date. The number of persons attend the classes before the one who attend class in Bhopal is one less than the number of persons after the one who attend the class in Delhi. N attends yoga class before S in the same month. Two persons attend the classes between S and the one who attend yoga class in Indore. The one who attends yoga class in Patna attends three persons before Q. R attends the yoga class after the one who attends yoga class in Lucknow. S neither attends class in Panipat nor in Ranchi.

 

On which date R attends yoga class?
questions.explanation:
Three persons attend the yoga classes between M and the one who attends the yoga class in Bhopal. M attends the yoga class in the month having even number of days. O attends just after the one who attends class in Bhopal. So, here we have three possible cases.

More than three persons attend the yoga classes between O and T. O and T attend the classes on the same date. So, case 3 gets eliminated here because no place left for T. The number of persons attend the classes before the one who attend class in Bhopal is one less than the number of persons after the one who attend the class in Delhi.

N attends yoga class before S in the same month. Two persons attend the classes between S and the one who attend yoga classes in Indore. So, case 2 gets eliminated here. The one who attends yoga classes in Patna attends three persons before Q. R attends the yoga class after the one who attends yoga class in Lucknow.

P is left only so, P attends class in Delhi. S neither attends class in Panipat nor in Ranchi which means S attends class in Haridwar. Thus the final arrangement is:

R attends the yoga class on 22 April.

questions.question: What is the result of converting the binary number 11010101 to decimal?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: A.

To convert the binary number 11010101 to decimal, we calculate the value of each bit based on its position, where each position represents a power of 2, starting from 0 on the right.

The binary number is 11010101, which has 8 bits. We assign each bit a position from right to left:

  • Bit 0: 1 (2^0 = 1)
  • Bit 1: 0 (2^1 = 2)
  • Bit 2: 1 (2^2 = 4)
  • Bit 3: 0 (2^3 = 8)
  • Bit 4: 1 (2^4 = 16)
  • Bit 5: 0 (2^5 = 32)
  • Bit 6: 1 (2^6 = 64)
  • Bit 7: 1 (2^7 = 128)

Now, multiply each bit by its corresponding power of 2 and sum the results where the bit is 1:

  • Bit 7: 1 * 128 = 128
  • Bit 6: 1 * 64 = 64
  • Bit 4: 1 * 16 = 16
  • Bit 2: 1 * 4 = 4
  • Bit 0: 1 * 1 = 1

Sum these values: 128 + 64 + 16 + 4 + 1 = 213

Thus, the binary number 11010101 converts to 213 in decimal.

Final Answer: 213

questions.question: Which entity has been designated as the operator (Payment System Operator, or PSO) for the Foreign Currency Settlement System (FCSS) launched by FM Nirmala Sitharaman at GIFT City’s International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) to enable real-time settlement of global currency transactions?

• The correct answer is option 'B' that is 'CCIL IFSC Ltd'.
  • Finance Minister launched the Foreign Currency Settlement System (FCSS) at GIFT City’s International Financial Services Centre (IFSC), enabling real-time settlement of global currency transactions.
  • CCIL IFSC Ltd, a subsidiary of Clearing Corporation of India, is the designated operator (Payment System Operator, or PSO) fer the FCSS. 
  • While the software is being developed by Indian Financial Technology & Allied Services (IFTAS), a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India.

Key Info: 

  • The FCSS is a real-time payment and settlement mechanism for transactions conducted in foreign currencies (initially in USD) within GIFT IFSC.
  • It replaces the older correspondent banking model, which required multiple intermediaries and 36–48 hours to process global transactions.
  • Under the FCSS, a local settlement bank (selected via bidding) will serve as the settlement hub. Member IFSC Banking Units (IBUs) will open accounts with this settlement bank.
  • Inter-bank foreign currency transactions will be settled directly via these accounts, bypassing the multi-leg Nostro chain.
  • The system will operate under the regulatory framework of the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007, and is authorised by IFSCA.

Additional Info:

  • The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) has been established on April 27, 2020 under the International Financial Services Centres Authority Act, 2019.
  • It is headquartered at GIFT City, Gandhinagar in Gujarat.
  • The IFSCA is a unified authority for the development and regulation of financial products, financial services and financial institutions in the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) in India.
  • At present, the GIFT IFSC is the maiden international financial services centre in India.
  • Prior to the establishment of IFSCA, the domestic financial regulators, namely, RBI, SEBI, PFRDA and IRDAI regulated the business in IFSC.

I know you've been preoccupied, but everyone else had noticed his interest in you.
questions.explanation:
The highlighted segment "had noticed his" is incorrect because "had noticed" is in the past perfect tense, which is used when referring to an action completed before another past action. However, there is no other past action that requires the use of past perfect.

The correct tense should be present perfect ("has noticed") because the sentence refers to something that is still relevant in the present.

Option Analysis:

  • A. has noticed his: (Correct – uses the present perfect tense correctly)
  • B. has noticing his: (Incorrect – "has" must be followed by past participle, not present participle)
  • C. has been noticed his: (Incorrect – "has been noticed" is passive, but the subject "everyone" is active)
  • D. have noticed his: (Incorrect – "everyone" is singular, so "has" should be used instead of "have")
  • E. No Correction required: (Incorrect – the original sentence has an incorrect tense usage)

Hence, option A is the correct choice.

The corrected sentence: I know you've been preoccupied, but everyone else has noticed his interest in you.

People who sit for hours on end develop chronic diseases, including diabetes, heart disease, dementia and several types of cancer at much higher rates from people who move throughout their day.
questions.explanation:
This sentence contains a grammatical error in the comparison structure. The phrase “at much higher rates from people” is incorrect. When comparing two groups, the correct word to use is “than”, not “from.”
Let’s go through the options:

Option (A): “at very high rate than” – This is incorrect because the phrase "very high" does not match the intended degree of comparison (which should be "much higher"), and also “rate” should be plural  "rates"  to match the context.

Option (B): “at most highest rate to” – This is grammatically incorrect because “most” and “highest” both indicate the superlative degree, so using them together is redundant. Also, “to” is not the correct preposition for comparison.

Option (C): “At much higher rate to” – This is incorrect because “rate” should be in the plural form “rates,” and again, “to” is not the correct preposition for comparison.

Option (D): “at much higher rates than” – This is the correct answer. The word “much” intensifies the comparison, “higher” is the comparative form, “rates” is correctly in plural, and “than” is the correct word to show comparison between the two groups of people.

B - Gender-based seat reservation is not

C - about discriminating against men

D - in the context of the systemic exclusion and

A - the injustices women have historically faced."

It then establishes the context (B) that gender-based seat reservation is not about discriminating against men (C) but rather about addressing the systemic exclusion and historical injustices faced by women (A).

Option (C) DCBEA - This option starts with part D, "Gender-based seat reservation is not," which is an incomplete and confusing beginning for the sentence. It doesn't provide the context or the counterargument needed to understand the argument's progression.

Option (D) CDEBA - This sequence starts with part C, "the injustices women have historically faced," which also lacks an introductory element to set up the counterargument. It jumps into the discussion without the necessary context and logic.
